questions.prompt: A 12 V source in series with 4 Ω feeds a 12 Ω resistor placed across the output terminals; the load will connect to the same terminals. Find the Thevenin resistance seen by the load, with the source replaced by a short. Enter a value and unit.

feedback.hint: With the source shorted, the 4 Ω and 12 Ω resistors are in parallel.
feedback.solution: Rth = (4 × 12)/(4 + 12) = 3 Ω. The Thevenin voltage is 12 × 12/16 = 9 V, so the load sees a 9 V source in series with 3 Ω.

questions.prompt: A sensor produces a 2 mV differential signal on top of a 1 V common-mode level. Which front end is most appropriate?
options: A passive attenuator.
A single inverting op-amp stage with unmatched resistors.
An instrumentation amplifier, which has high input impedance and a high common-mode rejection ratio.
A comparator.

feedback.hint: Ask what must be rejected and what must be preserved.
feedback.solution: The wanted signal is the small difference; the large common-mode level must be rejected. Instrumentation amplifiers combine high input impedance and high CMRR, and keep gain accurate for the difference.

questions.prompt: A signal contains components up to 150 Hz. What is the minimum sampling rate required by the Nyquist condition to avoid aliasing of that band? Enter a value and unit.

feedback.hint: The sampling rate must exceed twice the highest frequency.
feedback.solution: The minimum is 2 × 150 = 300 Hz, strictly greater in practice. Nyquist is necessary but not sufficient for real signals: noise above the band folds into it unless an anti-alias filter is used, and a filter's roll-off, the converter and timing jitter also matter.

questions.prompt: A voltage is calculated as V = I·R with I = 2.00 ± 0.02 A and R = 10.0 ± 0.1 Ω (independent standard uncertainties). Calculate the standard uncertainty of V. Enter a value and unit.

feedback.hint: For a product, relative uncertainties add in quadrature.
feedback.solution: V = 20.0 V. The relative uncertainties are 0.01 and 0.01, so the combined relative uncertainty is √(0.01² + 0.01²) = 0.0141 and the uncertainty is 20.0 × 0.0141 = 0.28 V.

questions.prompt: A data logger displays incubator temperature to 0.01 °C. Its thermistor divider has a 3% loading error at the logger input and the reference voltage drifts 1% over a day. Which statement is correct?
options: Loading error cancels out because it is constant.
The reading is accurate to 0.01 °C because that is what is displayed.
Reference drift does not affect ratiometric or non-ratiometric readings.
The display resolution does not reflect accuracy; the loading and reference errors dominate, so the reading can be off by much more than 0.01 °C.

feedback.hint: List each error in the same units and find the largest.
feedback.solution: Resolution is the step size of the display. Gain errors from loading and reference drift shift the reading by percent-level amounts. A constant loading error can be calibrated out only if calibration was done with the same input connected.

questions.prompt: Interference at 10 kHz passes this first-order filter at about 16% amplitude before 2000 Hz sampling. Which remedy addresses aliasing correctly?
options: Use a steeper (higher-order) analog filter or sample much faster and filter digitally, because content above f_s/2 cannot be removed after sampling.
Increase the amplifier gain.
Lower the sampling rate so less noise is collected.
Remove the interference digitally after sampling at 2,000 Hz.

feedback.hint: Aliased components look like real low-frequency signal once sampled.
feedback.solution: After sampling, aliased content is indistinguishable from signal, so suppression must happen before the converter, or the sampling rate must rise so that a digital filter can act before decimation.

feedback.hint: Keep gain, common-mode and drifting conditions separate while summarizing.
feedback.solution: Each group has three constructed outputs. Saturated groups remain at the exact stipulated rail because perturbations were applied before clipping.

questions.prompt: Settled low-gain groups at known −5 and +5 mV differential input have mean outputs 0.00 and 0.20 V with common mode zero. What gain in V/V follows? Enter the number only.

feedback.hint: Divide output difference by differential-input difference expressed in volts.
feedback.solution: Gain is (0.20−0.00)/(0.005−(−0.005))=20 V/V. These points are unsaturated.

questions.prompt: Settled high-gain groups at known −5 and +5 mV differential input have mean outputs −0.40 and +0.60 V. What unclipped gain in V/V follows? Enter the number only.

feedback.hint: Use the known unsaturated interior points rather than the ±15 mV plateaus.
feedback.solution: Gain is (0.60−(−0.40))/0.010=100 V/V. Fitting the clipped endpoints as ordinary linear points would compromise this result.

questions.prompt: At settled differential input zero, common modes −1 and +1 V give means 0.09 and 0.11 V. Combine their common-mode gain with differential gain 100. What amplitude CMRR in dB follows? Enter the number only.

feedback.hint: Estimate common-mode gain from the symmetric common-mode difference before taking 20log₁₀ of the gain ratio.
feedback.solution: Common-mode gain is (0.11−0.09)/2=0.010. CMRR=20log₁₀(100/0.010)=80 dB under the stipulated valid-range model.

questions.prompt: The separate zero-input drift condition has final baseline 0.10 V, initial mean 0.40 V and mean 0.210364 V at 0.50 s. Fit excess above baseline as Aexp(−t/τ). What τ in s follows approximately? Enter the number only.

feedback.hint: Subtract the final baseline before forming the remaining-excess ratio and logarithm.
feedback.solution: The excess ratio is approximately exp(−1), so τ≈0.50 s. Six-decimal report rounding produces a small difference from the exact construction.

response_fields.prompt: Which high-gain groups are appropriate for the declared affine gain/intercept fit?
options: The unsaturated −5,0,+5 mV groups at settled common mode zero.
All points including rail plateaus as though fully linear.
Only the largest clipped values, because their slope is most reliable.

response_fields.prompt: With offset 0.10 V,gain 100 and output rails ±1 V, what input limits follow at common mode zero?
options: −11 to +9 mV for the stipulated linear range.
Exactly −10 to +10 mV regardless of offset.
Unlimited input range because feedback removes rails.

response_fields.prompt: What does the separately stipulated drifting condition identify?
options: A conditional exponential baseline component, without unique real electrode-mechanism identification.
The same cause as every clipped movement signal.
A validated protocol change for a real subject.

evidence: Known interior references remain in the affine domain.
A nonzero offset creates asymmetric input headroom.
The construction separates state conditions and makes no real experiment claim.

feedback.hint: Keep linear-domain recovery, range constraints and causal interpretation distinct.
feedback.solution: Interior points identify the settled affine model, offset creates asymmetric headroom, and a separate exponential baseline does not uniquely diagnose a real interface.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the gain-sweep, common-mode and drift outputs are supported by their declared construction? Select all that apply.
options: The settled low-gain sweep remains unsaturated over all five supplied differential inputs.
A common-mode difference test identifies a separate leakage coefficient under the valid-range assumption.
Perturbations are deterministic and added before the stipulated output clamp.
A good exponential fit uniquely identifies a biological process.
Three repeated rail values prove the unclipped input amplitudes are equal.

feedback.hint: Use known inputs and model domains; do not infer lost information from plateaus.
feedback.solution: The constructed perturbations, low-gain domain and separate common-mode coefficient are supported. Repeated clipped values do not recover larger inputs, and an exponential does not uniquely identify biology.

questions.prompt: For high-gain inputs −15,−5,0,+5,+15 mV and means −1,−0.4,0.1,0.6,+1 V, what happens if all five are fit as one ordinary line?
options: The fit must recover exactly 100 because more points always improve a model.
The fit proves the settled source differential inputs changed.
The fit gives compromised gain 70 and intercept 0.06 V, unlike the interior calibration 100 and 0.10 V.

feedback.hint: Compare the assumed affine domain against known clipping limits.
feedback.solution: All-point OLS slope is 70 V/V and intercept 0.06 V. The clipped endpoint data violate the affine model; the unsaturated references retain the declared gain.
